findings.supported: Reported FY2025 segment revenues and segment operating results are separated and reconcile.
findings.counterArgument: Hospitality includes tourism/entertainment; reported result is not proven hotel EBITDA or normalized common-owner return.

findings.supported: Unallocated net income -4377507 million VND bridges segment result to consolidated pretax profit.
findings.counterArgument: This is profit, not operating cash. Segment working-capital/capex/cash realizations remain missing.

findings.supported: Reported assets and liabilities separated by segment with a distinct unallocated pool.
findings.counterArgument: Total liabilities are not interest-bearing debt. Funding, lease and claim allocations cannot follow revenue weights.

findings.supported: Two reported operating segments and material unallocated balances require separate economic models.
findings.counterArgument: Pooled group common cash DCF is unsuitable for acceptance until property/finance/corporate and preferred claims are separated.

findings.supported: Four exact arithmetic bridges reconcile segment revenue, results, assets and liabilities.
findings.counterArgument: Arithmetic reconciliation verifies reported data, not an independent economic valuation.

findings.supported: Eight named project contexts are identifiable in the inventory note.
findings.counterArgument: The source says mainly and other projects. It does not give exhaustive project GDV, ownership, remaining costs or timing.

findings.supported: Construction inventory pool 106955459 million VND is reported historical book cost.
findings.counterArgument: Sunk inventory cannot be treated as remaining cash capex, GDV or an equal allocation across projects.

findings.supported: The report identifies corporate deposits connected with potential projects.
findings.counterArgument: Recoverability, project rights, partner claims and debt allocation are not qualified; book equity cannot supply conservative RNAV.
